sections.label: 1 - SHOPIFY/WOOCOMMERCE CHATBOT: ORDERS AND PRODUCT QUESTIONS
sections.note: Your part 1, the Shopify/WooCommerce chatbot. One setting picks your platform, and order status and product answers come from your live store, never from Claude's memory.

sections.label: 2 - AUTOMATION TASK: LATE ORDERS FLAGGED TO YOU
sections.note: Your part 2, automation tasks, starting with this one. When a shopper asks about an order still unshipped past your shipping promise, you get an email before they ask twice.

sections.label: 3 - BUILDING AND IMPROVING WORKFLOWS: EVERY CHAT LOGGED
sections.note: Your part 3, building and improving workflows. Every chat lands in a Google Sheet with the question, the answer and whether a person was needed, so each improvement comes from real chats.

sections.note: Your part 4, connecting systems. Refunds, cancellations and anything the bot should not guess go to your inbox with the chat and the order, and your reply goes straight to the shopper.

sections.label: 5 - SUPPORTING ONGOING AUTOMATION NEEDS: NOTHING FAILS QUIETLY
sections.note: Your part 5, supporting ongoing automation needs. If any step fails, say a store key expires, you get the failed step and a link to the run.

nodes.label: 1 - Shopper Asks a Question in Your Store Chat
2 - Claude Sorts It: Order Status, Product Question or a Person

params.system_message: You read every message in an online store's chat and sort it before anything is looked up. The store runs on Shopify or WooCommerce; you never look anything up and never answer the shopper yourself. Return one intent: order_status (where is my order, has it shipped, tracking, delivery date) only when the chat so far has both an order number and the email used at checkout; need_details when they ask about an order but one of those two is missing; product_question (sizes, colours, materials, stock, price, which product to pick); human (refund, return, exchange, cancellation, damaged or wrong item, address change, payment problem, complaint, or they ask for a person); other (anything else, including empty or abusive messages). Read the earlier messages in this chat: an order number given two messages ago still counts. Set wants_person to true for human, and also when an order or product question comes with a refund, return, cancel or complaint request, and say why in handoff_reason in one short sentence. order_number is the number only, without the # sign. email is lowercase and exactly as typed; never guess or complete one. product_query is the few words a catalog search should match, such as linen pillow cover, and stays empty unless intent is product_question.
params.prompt:
=Shopper message: {{ $json.chatInput }}

Return intent, order_number, email, product_query, wants_person and handoff_reason.

nodes.label: 3 - Your Store: Shopify or WooCommerce?
nodes.notes: Flip one value in Config to move between Shopify and WooCommerce. Nothing else in the flow changes.

nodes.label: 4a - Shopify: Look Up the Order or the Product
nodes.notes: Orders older than 60 days need Shopify's read_all_orders scope, so older orders still get an answer.

params.url: https://{{ $('0 - Config: Your Settings').first().json.shopify_store }}.myshopify.com/admin/api/{{ $('0 - Config: Your Settings').first().json.shopify_api_version }}/graphql.json

body.query: query StoreLookup($orderQuery: String!, $productQuery: String!) { orders(first: 1, query: $orderQuery) { nodes { name email createdAt displayFinancialStatus displayFulfillmentStatus lineItems(first: 10) { nodes { title quantity } } fulfillments(first: 5) { status estimatedDeliveryAt trackingInfo(first: 3) { company number url } } } } products(first: 5, query: $productQuery) { nodes { title onlineStoreUrl totalInventory priceRangeV2 { minVariantPrice { amount currencyCode } } variants(first: 10) { nodes { title availableForSale } } } } }

nodes.label: 4b - WooCommerce: Look Up the Order or the Product
5 - One Shape for Either Store, Email Must Match
nodes.notes: Someone typing a stranger's order number gets nothing back. Your store decides what is true, never the model.

nodes.label: 6 - Claude Writes the Reply From Your Live Store Data

params.system_message: You write the reply a shopper sees in an online store's chat. Sound like a helpful person on the store's team: warm, plain words, no emojis, 2 to 4 sentences. Use only the store data you are given and never guess an order status, a delivery date, a price or stock. If intent is need_details, ask for the order number and the email used at checkout. If intent is order_status and order_found or email_matches is false, say you could not find an order with that number and email, ask them to check both, and share nothing else about any order. For a shipped order give the carrier, the tracking link and the delivery estimate when there is one. If late is true, say the order has not shipped yet, apologise once, and say the team has been told. For product_question answer from the products list only: name, price, in stock or not, and the link; if nothing matches, say so and offer to pass the question to the team. If wants_person is true, say a person from the team will email them within the reply time given, and ask for their email if shopper_email is empty. Never promise a refund, a cancellation, a discount or a delivery date the data does not show; a person decides those.
